result:
Debater A's case rests on a single citation, which they admit they have not checked. A claim that a constant is sharp needs more than a citation, and the sanity checks can't supply it.

K_n and G(n,q) are not extremal. At most, they show the bound isn't violated there, which is consistent with any constant at or above the true ratio on those graphs. Neither check shows that λ/(d_{3/2}√(n log n)) approaches 1 along any sequence.

For C = 1 to be "best possible," Debater A must exhibit graphs G_n with λ(G_n) ≥ (1−ε)·d_{3/2}(G_n)·√(n log n) for all large n. They offer no such family. Every family discussed so far, including the star, K_{n/2,n/2}, and K_n, gives a ratio of order 1/√(log n).

I concede that my own case for C = 0 is also built from examples, not a proof that the ratio vanishes for every sequence. The difference is in what each side must show. Debater A's answer of 1 is a claim of exact sharpness, which requires a matching extremal construction. None has been offered, so the positive claim is the one that lacks support.
